doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

title: Teaching at Berklee and advice to students
summary: Cecil McBee's tip led to a Berklee residency, now one and a half days a week; she lets students guide their own goals.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Do you find most of your colleagues do some educational type gigs?

A lot of them do, yeah. A lot of them do. In fact that’s how I get inspired to do it. It was Cecil McBee that told me about students in Boston. Because he teaches at the New England Conservatory and Berklee had called me up there to do a concert. And there was a clinic right before the concert. And it was an unbelievable clinic. I got these great questions, which I had never gotten before in a clinic. So then they called me to do a residency, but I was like, I can’t go there three days a week, no. So I told them I would do a half of a residency. So they found somebody. It took them about six months, but they found someone else to split it with. So I did that, and after I did that it was great teaching. I had just really great students. So I told them if they wanted I would teach one day a week if that would work in their program. And it did. So now I do one and a half days a week.
Yeah. Oh I wouldn’t move from New York.
The city I guess has a certain energy that’s just right for what you do.
Yeah I don’t know why I like it, I just do.
Is it possible to tell students something extra to prepare themselves to make a living with this kind of music?

Well they should be very serious about the music and if they are a student in school that’s what they really should be delving into. At the same time they should be thinking where they would like to present this music, how they would like to present it too. I don’t really teach that but if they ask me I certainly try to help them. A lot of them just want to teach as well, and then some want to perform. I try to just prepare them for what it is they think they want to do. I don’t tell them what they should do or what they want to do. I just kind of let them be the guide.
